task: RAG Retrieval Complementarity and Fusion Analysis

overall_task_success.commentary: The underlying numbers are entirely correct, and the ticket record names its own source files directly, a genuine strength worth crediting. The total time this took feels well out of proportion to me for one bounded computation and a fixed set of writes, and the extra minutes bought a repeated check that found nothing new. The recommendation ticket also leaves its related chunk identifiers as one undifferentiated list instead of tying each one to the specific case it supports, so I still have to do that tracing by hand. Correct math and traceable tickets still leave me a handoff that took too long to produce and needs manual reassembly before I could hand it to someone else.

task_accuracy.commentary: The disputed rows stay flagged instead of quietly resolved, a corpus gap never gets confused with a plain retrieval miss, and checking the source rankings myself, every query lands in the right bucket. The sweep across the full weighting range lands on the right optimum, and the recall and improvement figures hold up against my own recompute. The sheet carries no legend explaining what the categories mean or how the fusion score gets built, so it only makes sense to a reader with the original brief. Nothing in the closing message mentions four specific queries buried in its own numbers, rows where a plain keyword match alone would have worked but the chosen fusion setting drops them anyway.

efficiency.wrong_actions_recovery: the same summary tab gets opened and read a second time and turns up nothing new before the check is called done, otherwise nothing wrong.
efficiency.commentary: When I check it end to end, 6.8 minutes feels past what a bounded computation over a fixed query log and a fixed set of writes should need, and the extra time doesn't buy me a larger result. I can see it includes a pass at opening the rendered sheet to look for layout problems, a useful step, but that pass turns up nothing and gets repeated on the same tab without new information before moving on. A repeated look at the same screen with no new finding is the kind of drag that adds minutes without adding value, and on a task this bounded I'd expect the total time to track the scope more closely than it does here.

writing_quality.commentary: The closing message lays out the retrieval numbers, the full sweep, and the category rollup each in a labeled table, and nothing in it is hard for me to follow. Presenting the headline recall figures and the full sweep as two separate tables means the same optimal weight row gets repeated with overlapping numbers, so I end up reconciling two tables that say the same thing. The nine finished tickets get dumped into a plain two line list of comma separated keys instead of the clean table treatment the numbers get, breaking the pattern the rest of the message sets up. To me it reads competently but closer to a data dump than a considered narrative.

instruction_following.commentary: Walking the brief's constraints one by one, I find every one honored, the row count, the ban on merging similar queries, the boundary against altering production retrieval, and the separation of a corpus gap from a retrieval miss that only happened to miss in the top five. This run never says whether category recall gets computed against the category's own count or the full log, two bases that would land on different numbers, it picks one silently. The six disputed queries get counted through a convention, treating either candidate chunk as a hit, but that convention never appears in the deliverable. Both calls turn out reasonable to me, but resolving two ambiguities without naming either one is a genuine gap.

collaboration_autonomy_verification.steering_needed: none. It went start to finish on the one prompt without stopping once.
collaboration_autonomy_verification.additional_editing: not much on substance, mainly tightening the repeated tables in the closing summary before I'd send it anywhere.
collaboration_autonomy_verification.commentary: I can see this run opens the finished sheet and reads the rendered tabs before calling itself done, a real content level check rather than a confirmation that a write request succeeded. It runs a final reconciliation across all 84 rows, the four rollup rows, and the category and flag counts, catching any internal mismatch before handing the work back. The one place this thoroughness doesn't reach for me is Jira. After filing all nine tickets, the closing check confirms they exist through a search rather than reading a ticket's body to check its finding and recommended action against the sheet. That gap, on an otherwise carefully verified close, keeps this just short of the top of the band.

citation_quality.commentary: Both tickets I opened name the exact source files behind the analysis directly in the ticket body, a concrete and traceable habit, and every headline number traces cleanly back to the source when I check it myself. Where this comes up short is that the related query and chunk identifiers in the recommendation record are listed as one undifferentiated block rather than mapped to which specific hybrid recovery or which specific retrieval miss each one supports, so tracing an individual case still takes manual work. The improvement is also reported only as a relative percentage, without the plain point gap alongside it.

gui_action_correctness.commentary: When I trace the path, the rendered sheet gets opened and read correctly, no wrong clicks or misdirected navigation anywhere in the pass. Getting there took several stops though, opening the sheet, loading the workbook, and checking rendering as three steps before the tab level look begins, more page turns than I'd need for a direct open and scan. That tab level look then only shows me the category summary tab inspected, twice in a row, with no step anywhere showing the detail tab getting the same look, even though the closing claim covers both tabs as confirmed legible. A single pass through both tabs once each would have covered the same ground with a shorter, more complete route.
